copilot-in-app.definition: Copilot in an app brings AI help to where people already work, such as SharePoint sites, files, pages, and lists.

blocks.label: Copilot in SharePoint
blocks.plain: AI help inside SharePoint for questions, content, and files.

blocks.label: Everyday work
blocks.plain: Included with the Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

blocks.label: Advanced work
blocks.plain: Larger jobs that use Copilot Credits through usage-based billing.

blocks.label: Site AI settings
blocks.plain: Choices that site owners make about AI on their site.

blocks.label: Restricted discovery
blocks.plain: A site setting that hides AI entry points and content.

flow.label: Work
flow.plain: A person with a Copilot license works in a SharePoint site.

flow.label: Ask
flow.plain: They ask Copilot a question or request a page, list, or file.

flow.label: Respond
flow.plain: Copilot works with the site's content to answer or create.

flow.label: Larger jobs
flow.plain: For advanced work, Copilot asks before it spends Copilot Credits.

flow.label: Limits
flow.plain: If the site restricts AI, Copilot does not appear there.

example.input: A Contoso site owner asks Copilot to draft a new page about the team offsite.
example.output: Copilot drafts a page in the site, using the request and the site's content.

whenToUse: People already work in SharePoint and want help with their content.
You want to create pages, lists, or files with natural language.
A large content job might call for advanced work.
whenNot: Advanced work needs usage-based billing and Copilot Credits.
Some government clouds and other environments do not support it yet.
Prompts work best in languages that both SharePoint and Copilot support.
copilot-in-app.needToKnow: Everyday help in SharePoint comes with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Larger, automated jobs are called advanced work and use Copilot Credits. Site owners and administrators can limit where Copilot shows up.
copilot-in-app.demo: Show a SharePoint site where Copilot answers a question and drafts a page from the site's content.
copilot-in-app.askTheRoom: What do people on your site spend the most time doing: finding content, writing it, or organizing it?
copilot-in-app.sayOutLoud: Many Contoso teams already keep their files, pages, and lists in SharePoint. Copilot in SharePoint helps them where they already work: ask a question, draft a page, or build a list, all in plain language.

quiz.q: What do everyday Copilot in SharePoint features require?
quiz.why: Everyday capabilities are included with the Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

quiz.q: What do advanced work features use?
quiz.why: Advanced work needs usage-based billing and available Copilot Credits.

quiz.q: What does a site with Restricted Content Discovery show?
options: No Copilot button or AI entry points
A second copy of the site
quiz.why: If Restricted Content Discovery is on, Copilot in SharePoint and AI actions do not appear on that site.

learn.title: Get started with Copilot in SharePoint
Restrict discovery of SharePoint sites and content

fdy-orient-foundry.definition: Orienting means learning the two Foundry portals, then picking a first build: a prompt agent, a hosted agent, or a direct model call.

blocks.label: Prompt agent
blocks.plain: You set instructions, a model, and tools. Foundry hosts and runs it.

blocks.label: Hosted agent
blocks.plain: Your own code or framework, packaged so Foundry can run it.

blocks.label: Model call
blocks.plain: A prompt sent straight to a model, with no tools or orchestration.

blocks.label: Two portals
blocks.plain: The new portal shows Foundry projects. The classic portal shows all project types.

flow.label: Sign in
flow.plain: A person opens Foundry and sees which portal version they are in.

flow.label: Set a goal
flow.plain: They decide whether they want an agent or just a model response.

flow.label: Pick a style
flow.plain: For an agent, they pick declarative (prompt agent) or full code (hosted agent).

flow.label: Grow
flow.plain: They can start declarative and move to code as their needs grow.

example.input: A Contoso developer wants a first agent with the least to manage.
example.output: A prompt agent: instructions, a model, and tools that Foundry hosts and runs, with no application code or containers to maintain.

whenToUse: You want an agent with no runtime to manage: pick a prompt agent.
You have your own agent code: pick a hosted agent.
You only need to send prompts to a model: use a single call.
whenNot: If instructions and tools are enough, a prompt agent is simpler.
A single model call has no tools or orchestration. It is not an agent.

learn.title: What is Microsoft Foundry?
Microsoft Foundry product and capability map

fdy-create-hub-based-project.definition: A hub-based project lives in a hub, an Azure resource whose settings are shared by all the projects inside it.

blocks.label: Hub
blocks.plain: An Azure resource that holds shared settings for a group of projects.

blocks.label: Project
blocks.plain: One team's workspace, created inside a hub in the classic portal.

blocks.label: Connections
blocks.plain: Links to outside data and models. Hubs share them; projects can add their own.

blocks.label: Supporting services
blocks.plain: Storage and secret storage, set up once per hub for its projects.

flow.label: Hub
flow.plain: Someone creates a hub, or a default hub is made with the first project.

flow.label: Project
flow.plain: A project is created inside the hub, in the hub's location.

flow.label: Settings pass down
flow.plain: Security settings set on the hub pass down to every project.

flow.label: Build
flow.plain: The team builds in the project, using hub-only features if they need them.

example.input: Contoso wants several teams to share one set of security settings and connections.
example.output: One hub holds the shared settings. Each team gets its own hub-based project that follows them.

whenToUse: You need features only hubs have, such as prompt flow.
You want shared security settings and connections for many projects.
An admin team already built a hub for you.
whenNot: Learn calls this legacy support and describes how to move to a Foundry project.
New agents and model features are built for Foundry projects.
fdy-create-hub-based-project.dataNote: Projects in a hub share its security settings, but their files and secrets are kept apart.

learn.title: Hub resources overview (classic)
Create a hub project for Microsoft Foundry (classic)

fdy-explore-model-catalog.definition: The model catalog lets you search thousands of models, read each model card, and pick one sold by Azure or from a partner.

blocks.label: Sold by Azure
blocks.plain: Microsoft hosts and sells these, with Microsoft support and service level agreements.

blocks.label: Partners and community
blocks.plain: Most models. Providers build and support them, and often check them themselves.

blocks.label: Filters
blocks.plain: Narrow the list by provider, region, features, and task.

blocks.label: Model card
blocks.plain: Quick facts, details, deployments, benchmarks, and license for one model.

flow.label: Search
flow.plain: A person searches by keyword or narrows the list with filters.

flow.label: Read
flow.plain: They read the model card for facts, benchmarks, and the license.

flow.label: Compare
flow.plain: They compare models using leaderboard and benchmark data, where it exists.

flow.label: Decide
flow.plain: They weigh Azure support against partner innovation and pick a model.

example.input: Fabrikam needs a model that can reason through hard questions and call tools.
example.output: A shortlist of models with those features. Each model card helps the team check benchmarks, license, and region.

whenToUse: You need guaranteed Microsoft support: look at models sold by Azure.
You need a niche or very new capability: look at partner and community models.
whenNot: You are responsible for choosing a model that fits your use case.
Models from other providers follow the terms that come with them.

learn.title: Overview of Microsoft Foundry Models

fdy-manage-quota.definition: Quota is the usage allowance Azure gives you for each model and region, in tokens per minute, which you can view, share out, and ask to raise.

blocks.label: Allowance
blocks.plain: The total tokens per minute Azure gives your subscription for one model and region.

blocks.label: Deployment share
blocks.plain: The part of that allowance you give to each deployment.

blocks.label: Shared pool
blocks.plain: A shared pool for temporary test endpoints. It is not for production.

blocks.label: Request
blocks.plain: A request for more quota when you reach your limit.

flow.label: View
flow.plain: A person with the right role views quota and usage for each deployment.

flow.label: Notice
flow.plain: They see that a deployment, or a new one, needs more than is left.

flow.label: Free up
flow.plain: They move unused quota from other deployments to the one that needs it.

flow.label: Request
flow.plain: If that is not enough, they submit a request for more quota.

flow.label: Wait
flow.plain: Changes can take up to 15 minutes to show.

example.input: A Contoso team's new deployment fails because the model has no quota left.
example.output: The team frees tokens from a deployment it no longer uses, or requests more quota, then deploys again.

whenToUse: A deployment fails because no quota is left.
You want to give a busy deployment a bigger share.
You want to see usage across projects in one subscription.
whenNot: Shared quota is only for temporary tests, not production endpoints.
Some model and region pairs do not allow quota increases.

learn.title: Manage and increase quotas for resources with Microsoft Foundry

dca-agent-builder-vs-copilot-studio.definition: Copying an Agent Builder agent to Copilot Studio makes a separate snapshot that adds features but does not stay in sync.

blocks.label: Original
blocks.plain: Stays available in Microsoft 365 Copilot after the copy.

blocks.label: Snapshot
blocks.plain: A copy kept in Copilot Studio. Edits to the original do not reach it.

blocks.label: Copied items
blocks.plain: Name, description, instructions, suggested prompts, icon, and SharePoint and website knowledge.

blocks.label: Not copied
blocks.plain: Some knowledge, such as embedded files and connector content, needs rework.

flow.label: Outgrow
flow.plain: An Agent Builder agent needs workflows, outside actions, or more channels.

flow.label: Copy
flow.plain: The owner copies it into a Copilot Studio environment that stores agents.

flow.label: Rework
flow.plain: Items that did not copy, such as embedded files, are set up again.

flow.label: Test
flow.plain: The owner tests the copy before publishing it.

flow.label: Decide
flow.plain: The owner decides whether to delete the original and tells its users.

example.input: Contoso's onboarding agent now needs a workflow that updates another system.
example.output: A Copilot Studio copy with the same instructions and supported knowledge, ready for workflows. Embedded files must be uploaded again.

whenToUse: An Agent Builder agent needs workflows, connectors, or more channels.
You want versioning, staged deployments, and analytics.
whenNot: Each copy creates a new agent, so avoid copying again and again.
Do not expect the copy to follow later changes to the original.

learn.title: Copy an agent from Agent Builder to Copilot Studio
Choose between Agent Builder and Copilot Studio to build your agent

m365h-control-web-search.definition: Web search lets Copilot add fresh public web facts to its answers, if a company allows it and the person leaves it on.

blocks.label: Search query
blocks.plain: A few words Copilot builds from the prompt and sends to Bing.

blocks.label: Web content
blocks.plain: Public results that Copilot can add to an answer.

blocks.label: Company choice
blocks.plain: Web search can be allowed or turned off for people or groups.

blocks.label: Personal switch
blocks.plain: A toggle people use to leave web content out of answers.

blocks.label: Query citations
blocks.plain: A list of the exact web queries sent, shown in Copilot Chat.

flow.label: Ask
flow.plain: A person asks Copilot a question.

flow.label: Check
flow.plain: Copilot checks whether web search is allowed and would improve the answer.

flow.label: Query
flow.plain: If so, it builds a short search query and sends it to Bing.

flow.label: Answer
flow.plain: It combines web results with work data the person can access.

flow.label: Show
flow.plain: Copilot Chat lists the web queries it used.

example.input: A Contoso employee asks Copilot to compare an internal document with Fabrikam's public news.
example.output: Copilot sends Bing only a short query about Fabrikam, not the document. The answer combines the document with public results.

whenToUse: You want answers that include current public information.
Your company needs a clear rule about public web use in Copilot.
Auditors want to see which web queries Copilot sent.
whenNot: A company may turn it off to follow its own policies or laws.
With web search off, answers can be less up to date.
m365h-control-web-search.dataNote: Bing works separately from Microsoft 365 and has its own data-handling rules. Learn lists commitments for these queries, such as no use to train generative AI foundation models.

learn.title: Data, privacy, and security for web search in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat

m365h-restrict-copilot-chat-access.definition: Managing Copilot Chat access means choosing who may use it, such as only licensed people.

blocks.label: Sign-in account
blocks.plain: Work or school accounts get enterprise protections. Personal accounts stay separate.

blocks.label: Where it appears
blocks.plain: Copilot Chat shows in the Copilot app, Teams, Outlook, and on the web.

blocks.label: Blocking
blocks.plain: A block can cover chosen users or groups, including licensed users.

blocks.label: Blocked message
blocks.plain: Blocked people see that Copilot Chat is off, with an optional company link.

flow.label: Decide
flow.plain: A company decides who should have Copilot Chat.

flow.label: Limit
flow.plain: It limits or blocks access for the people who should not.

flow.label: Blocked
flow.plain: A blocked person who opens Copilot Chat sees a note that it is off.

flow.label: Guidance
flow.plain: The note can link to company guidance.

example.input: Fabrikam wants Copilot Chat only for people who hold a Copilot license.
example.output: The Copilot app and Teams chat stop reaching unlicensed people, and licensed people keep access.

whenToUse: A group is not ready for Copilot Chat yet.
Company policy limits who may use AI chat.
whenNot: A block that covers everyone also stops people with a Copilot license.
Unpinning Copilot Chat does not stop people from reaching it on the web.

learn.title: Manage Copilot Chat

m365h-troubleshoot-copilot-access.definition: Troubleshooting access means finding why someone cannot reach Copilot, such as blocked web addresses, the wrong account, or a new change.

blocks.label: Network rules
blocks.plain: Rules that block Copilot's web addresses can stop it from loading.

blocks.label: Account type
blocks.plain: Work or school and personal accounts get different experiences and protections.

blocks.label: Timing
blocks.plain: Policy changes, such as pinning, can take up to 48 hours.

blocks.label: Diagnostics logs
blocks.plain: Details an admin can send to Microsoft for people who cannot send feedback.

flow.label: Report
flow.plain: A person reports that Copilot will not open or is missing.

flow.label: Account
flow.plain: The helper checks which kind of account the person signed in with.

flow.label: Network
flow.plain: Next they check whether network rules block Copilot's web addresses.

flow.label: Wait
flow.plain: They allow time if a policy changed recently.

flow.label: Escalate
flow.plain: If it still fails, they send diagnostic logs to Microsoft.

example.input: A Contoso employee says Copilot Chat will not load on the office network.
example.output: The first checks are whether network rules block Copilot's web addresses and whether the person signed in with a work account.

whenToUse: Someone cannot reach Copilot but should be able to.
A new policy should be in effect but is not working yet.
whenNot: A 'turned off for your organization' note means a block, not a fault.
Diagnostics logs can include prompts and responses, so review them first.

learn.title: Manage Copilot Chat
Configure Microsoft Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center

m365h-pin-copilot-chat.definition: Pinning puts Copilot Chat in the navigation bar of Microsoft 365 apps such as Teams and Outlook, so people find it quickly.

blocks.label: Pinned chat
blocks.plain: Copilot Chat shown in the navigation bar of an app.

blocks.label: Teams pinning
blocks.plain: Teams has its own way to pin and allow apps.

blocks.label: Personal choice
blocks.plain: A person who sees it pinned can unpin it, and it stays unpinned.

blocks.label: Taskbar
blocks.plain: The Copilot app can also be pinned to the Windows taskbar on managed devices.

flow.label: Decide
flow.plain: A company decides whether Copilot Chat is pinned.

flow.label: Default
flow.plain: For most eligible people it is pinned by default.

flow.label: Personal
flow.plain: A person who prefers can unpin it.

flow.label: Wait
flow.plain: Changes to the company choice can take up to 48 hours.

example.input: Contoso wants people to find Copilot Chat in Teams and Outlook without searching.
example.output: Copilot Chat appears in the navigation bar of those apps, and people can still unpin it themselves.

whenToUse: You want people to find Copilot Chat quickly.
You want the Copilot app on the Windows taskbar of managed devices.
whenNot: Pinning is about visibility. It does not give or remove access.
Only people with a work or school account can have it pinned.

learn.title: Pin Microsoft Copilot Chat in the Microsoft 365 apps

m365h-agent-management-rules.definition: Agent management rules find agents that meet a condition, show which ones will change, and then act on many agents at once.

blocks.label: Condition
blocks.plain: What an agent must match for the rule to apply.

blocks.label: Review
blocks.plain: A list of affected agents to check before the rule runs.

blocks.label: Bulk action
blocks.plain: The change applied to every chosen agent at once.

blocks.label: Tags
blocks.plain: Labels, up to 50 per organization, that make agents easier to find.

blocks.label: Feedback sharing
blocks.plain: A choice about whether developers get ratings and comments.

flow.label: Define
flow.plain: An administrator defines which agents a rule should find.

flow.label: List
flow.plain: The rule lists the matching agents.

flow.label: Review
flow.plain: The administrator reviews the list and picks all or some.

flow.label: Run
flow.plain: The rule runs one action, such as blocking or reassigning.

example.input: Fabrikam wants to block old agents that have no owner and no usage.
example.output: A rule finds ownerless agents with no use, shows the list, and blocks the ones the administrator confirms.

whenToUse: You need to act on many agents, not one at a time.
You want to apply the same safety template to existing agents.
You want to organize agents with tags.
whenNot: Rules that reassign owners only cover agents made in Agent Builder.
A template rule runs once. It is not a schedule.

learn.title: Agent settings in Microsoft 365 admin center

m365h-data-access-governance-reports.definition: Data access governance reports show which SharePoint and OneDrive sites are shared too widely, today and over the last 28 days.

blocks.label: Snapshot reports
blocks.plain: Show who can reach each site as of the day you run them.

blocks.label: Activity reports
blocks.plain: Show new sharing links and wide sharing in the last 28 days.

blocks.label: Site permissions
blocks.plain: Finds sites open to thousands of people, guests, or everyone inside.

blocks.label: Label report
blocks.plain: Finds sites that hold files with chosen sensitivity labels.

blocks.label: Fixes
blocks.plain: Options such as limiting access to a group or asking site owners to review.

flow.label: Snapshot
flow.plain: An admin runs a snapshot report to see how widely sites are shared.

flow.label: Find sites
flow.plain: The report lists the sites with the broadest access.

flow.label: Watch activity
flow.plain: Activity reports add recent sharing, so new risks show early.

flow.label: Fix
flow.plain: The administrator chooses a fix, such as asking site owners to review.

flow.label: Repeat
flow.plain: Reports run again later to check progress.

example.input: Contoso wants to know which sites everyone in the company can open.
example.output: A report lists sites shared with everyone inside the company, so the team can pick which to review first.

whenToUse: You are preparing for Copilot and need to find sites open too widely.
You want to catch new oversharing as it happens.
whenNot: Reports find risk. They do not change access on their own.
Reports need SharePoint Advanced Management prerequisites, which Learn lists.

learn.title: Data access governance reports for SharePoint and OneDrive sites

m365h-restricted-content-discovery.definition: This setting keeps chosen SharePoint sites out of company-wide search and Copilot answers, without changing who has access.

blocks.label: Site setting
blocks.plain: A setting applied to one SharePoint site.

blocks.label: Hidden content
blocks.plain: The site's content stays out of organization-wide search and Copilot.

blocks.label: Permissions
blocks.plain: Unchanged. People who already have access can still open the content.

blocks.label: AI buttons
blocks.plain: AI entry points, such as the Copilot button, are removed on that site.

blocks.label: Reports and audit
blocks.plain: Administrators can report on which sites use it and audit changes.

flow.label: Mark
flow.plain: An administrator marks a site as restricted.

flow.label: Spread
flow.plain: Search systems pass the setting along, which can take time.

flow.label: Hidden
flow.plain: The site's content stops showing up in company-wide search and Copilot answers.

flow.label: Access
flow.plain: People with access still open the files directly.

flow.label: Remove
flow.plain: Later, the restriction is removed once access is reviewed.

example.input: Contoso wants to review Finance and HR site permissions before Copilot can surface them.
example.output: Those sites drop out of Copilot answers and company-wide search during the review. They return when the restriction ends.

whenToUse: Sites carry a high risk of oversharing.
A phased Copilot rollout needs more time for review.
whenNot: Too much use can leave Copilot answers thin and less useful.
It does not stop Copilot from summarizing a file someone already has open.
It applies to SharePoint sites only, not OneDrive.
m365h-restricted-content-discovery.dataNote: It does not remove content from the search index, so other Microsoft Purview tools still work on it.

learn.title: Restrict discovery of SharePoint sites and content

m365h-dlp-for-copilot.definition: A Data Loss Prevention (DLP) rule can stop Copilot from using sensitive prompts or labeled files.

blocks.label: Rule target
blocks.plain: The Copilot experiences that the rule covers.

blocks.label: Sensitive info
blocks.plain: Patterns such as card, passport, or Social Security numbers.

blocks.label: Labels
blocks.plain: Tags on files and emails that Copilot can be told to skip.

blocks.label: Action
blocks.plain: What Copilot is stopped from doing, such as answering or searching the web.

flow.label: Prompt
flow.plain: A person writes a prompt, or Copilot gathers files and emails to answer.

flow.label: Check
flow.plain: The rule checks the prompt or content for sensitive data or labels.

flow.label: Block
flow.plain: On a match, Copilot is blocked from that use.

flow.label: Fall back
flow.plain: For web search, Copilot still answers from allowed internal sources.

example.input: Contoso does not want customer card numbers sent to a web search provider.
example.output: When a prompt has card numbers, Copilot skips web search and answers only from allowed internal Microsoft 365 data.

whenToUse: You must keep sensitive numbers out of prompts and web searches.
You want labeled files and emails kept out of Copilot answers.
whenNot: One rule cannot check both sensitive data and labels.
Learn marks some of these controls as preview, so check their status.

learn.title: Use Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention to protect interactions with Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Cowork

m365h-audit-copilot-interactions.definition: Audit logs record each Copilot and agent interaction: who used it, when, where, and which files or sites it used to answer.

blocks.label: Audit record
blocks.plain: One log entry for an interaction, made automatically.

blocks.label: Details
blocks.plain: Facts such as the app, the agent, and the resources it used.

blocks.label: Label info
blocks.plain: Whether Copilot touched a file that has a sensitivity label.

blocks.label: Web search
blocks.plain: Whether Copilot searched the web, and the exact queries.

flow.label: Use
flow.plain: A person uses Copilot or an agent.

flow.label: Log
flow.plain: The system logs the interaction automatically.

flow.label: Search
flow.plain: An administrator searches the logs.

flow.label: Read
flow.plain: They read details such as who, when, which agent, and which files.

flow.label: Check web
flow.plain: They can also check whether web search was used.

example.input: Fabrikam's compliance team asks which files Copilot used for one answer.
example.output: The audit record lists the user, the time, the app, and the files or sites Copilot accessed.

whenToUse: You need evidence of how Copilot and agents are used.
You are investigating a possible data leak.
whenNot: Auditing must be on for the organization. No extra Copilot setup is needed.
Logs for non-Microsoft AI apps use pay-as-you-go billing.

learn.title: Audit logs for Copilot and AI applications

m365h-dspm-copilot-risk.definition: A Microsoft Purview dashboard shows where sensitive data is, who can reach it, and how well it is guarded, even for Copilot and agents.

blocks.label: Dashboard
blocks.plain: A dashboard of key data security measures and 30-day trends.

blocks.label: Goals
blocks.plain: Goals such as preventing oversharing, each with guided steps.

blocks.label: AI app list
blocks.plain: A list of AI apps and agents with recent activity and risk.

blocks.label: Activity view
blocks.plain: A view of AI activity, including prompts, responses, and sensitive content.

blocks.label: Risk checks
blocks.plain: Checks that find possible oversharing and suggest fixes.

flow.label: Use
flow.plain: People use Copilot and agents as usual.

flow.label: Scan
flow.plain: The service keeps scanning for sensitive data and risky activity.

flow.label: Dashboards
flow.plain: Dashboards show risk, policy coverage, and trends.

flow.label: Review
flow.plain: An administrator reviews suggested actions for each goal.

flow.label: Act
flow.plain: They apply policies or start investigations, and track progress.

example.input: Contoso wants to know which agents handle sensitive data.
example.output: A list of agents with recent activity, showing how many are high risk and how many touched sensitive data.

whenToUse: You want one view of data risk across Copilot, agents, and data.
You want guided steps to reduce oversharing.
whenNot: A new setup needs about a day before data appears.
Some capabilities need extra roles or licenses.

learn.title: Learn about Data Security Posture Management

ppai-check-region-and-prerequisites.definition: Before you build, check which AI Builder models your region offers and that your environment has what it needs.

blocks.label: Region
blocks.plain: Models run in the region that hosts your environment.

blocks.label: Release status
blocks.plain: Each model is generally available or in preview in a region.

blocks.label: Environment
blocks.plain: A Power Platform environment with a Dataverse database.

blocks.label: License
blocks.plain: An AI Builder license, trial or paid, for features that need one.

flow.label: Find region
flow.plain: A maker notes the region of their environment.

flow.label: Look up
flow.plain: They look up each model they want in that region's table.

flow.label: Read marks
flow.plain: A dash means the model is not available there.

flow.label: Check status
flow.plain: They note whether it is generally available or in preview.

flow.label: Confirm
flow.plain: They confirm the environment has a database and the right license.

example.input: Fabrikam wants to use a model, but its environment is in a region that may not offer it.
example.output: The table shows if the model is offered there, and if it is generally available or in preview.

whenToUse: You are planning a project around one model.
A model you expected is missing from the list.
whenNot: Prompt availability is listed on a separate page.
Preview features are not meant for production use.

learn.title: Feature availability by region

ppai-migrate-from-text-generation.definition: The Text generation model is retired, and Learn points makers to prompts in prompt builder instead.

blocks.label: Old model
blocks.plain: An older preview model, deprecated and no longer visible.

blocks.label: Prompt builder
blocks.plain: The replacement: you write a prompt, add inputs, and test it.

blocks.label: Renamed actions
blocks.plain: Some flow actions have new names since May 2025.

blocks.label: Existing work
blocks.plain: Flows and apps that used the old model should move to prompts.

flow.label: Spot it
flow.plain: A maker finds an older flow or app that mentions text generation.

flow.label: Recognize
flow.plain: They recognize that the model is retired.

flow.label: Rebuild
flow.plain: They recreate the task as a prompt in prompt builder.

flow.label: Test
flow.plain: They test the prompt with sample inputs.

flow.label: Switch
flow.plain: They point the flow or app at the new prompt.

example.input: Contoso has an old flow that used text generation to summarize emails.
example.output: The task becomes a prompt that takes the email text as an input. The flow runs that prompt instead of the retired model.

whenToUse: You find an old flow or app that uses text generation.
You need generated text in a flow or app today.
whenNot: Do not start new work on the retired Text generation model.
Prompts run only in some regions, so check availability first.

learn.title: Text generation model (preview) (deprecated)
Use your prompt in Power Automate

ppai-prebuilt-sentiment-analysis.definition: The sentiment analysis model reads text and says if it sounds positive, negative, neutral, or mixed.

blocks.label: Text input
blocks.plain: Text up to 5,120 characters, in a supported language.

blocks.label: Document result
blocks.plain: An overall label: positive, negative, neutral, or mixed.

blocks.label: Sentence results
blocks.plain: A label and a confidence score for each sentence.

blocks.label: Confidence
blocks.plain: A value from 0 to 1. Closer to 1 means more sure.

flow.label: Send text
flow.plain: A person, a flow, or an app gives the model some text.

flow.label: Read
flow.plain: The model reads the text sentence by sentence.

flow.label: Score
flow.plain: It scores each sentence as positive, negative, or neutral.

flow.label: Combine
flow.plain: The sentence scores add up to a label for the whole document.

flow.label: Use
flow.plain: The flow or app uses the label and scores.

example.input: A review: 'Fast shipping, but the box was damaged.'
example.output: A label for the whole review, plus a label and confidence score for each of the two sentences.

whenToUse: You want to sort reviews, social posts, or emails by tone.
You need scores for each sentence and for the whole text.
whenNot: It will not sort text into your own custom categories.
One call cannot take text longer than 5,120 characters.

learn.title: Sentiment analysis prebuilt model

ppai-prebuilt-receipt-processing-flow.definition: The receipt processing model reads printed and handwritten receipts and returns fields such as merchant, date, and total.

blocks.label: Receipt file
blocks.plain: An image or PDF of one receipt. One clear photo or scan works best.

blocks.label: Fields
blocks.plain: Merchant, date, time, items, subtotal, tax, tip, and total.

blocks.label: Confidence
blocks.plain: A score for each field shows how sure the model is.

blocks.label: Page range
blocks.plain: For long files, you can point the model at the pages with the receipt.

flow.label: Start
flow.plain: A flow starts with a receipt file.

flow.label: Send
flow.plain: The flow sends the file to the receipt model.

flow.label: Read
flow.plain: The model reads printed and handwritten text and finds key fields.

flow.label: Return
flow.plain: It returns the values as text, with confidence scores.

flow.label: Use
flow.plain: Later steps in the flow use those values.

example.input: A Contoso employee sends a photo of a lunch receipt for an expense report.
example.output: The flow reads the merchant, date, and total from the receipt and passes them to later steps in the flow.

whenToUse: You process expense receipts that arrive as photos or scans.
You want fields pulled out without training a model.
whenNot: It does not handle receipts that span several pages.
Other document types may need invoice processing or a custom model.

learn.title: Receipt processing prebuilt model
Use the receipt processing prebuilt model in Power Automate

ppai-powerfx-ai-models-in-canvas-app.definition: Power Fx lets a canvas app call an AI Builder model with a short formula, such as one that finds the language of text a person typed.

blocks.label: Data source
blocks.plain: The AI model added to the app so formulas can reach it.

blocks.label: Formula
blocks.plain: A Power Fx formula that calls the model and reads its result.

blocks.label: Control
blocks.plain: A text box, label, or button that shows or triggers the result.

blocks.label: Saved result
blocks.plain: A stored result, so the app can reuse it without calling again.

flow.label: Type
flow.plain: A person types text into the app.

flow.label: Trigger
flow.plain: A button or action runs the formula.

flow.label: Predict
flow.plain: The model returns a result, such as a language code.

flow.label: Show
flow.plain: A label shows the result.

example.input: A person types 'bonjour' into a Contoso app.
example.output: The app shows the language code for French.

whenToUse: You build a canvas app and want AI results in its controls.
You want to reuse one model result in several places.
whenNot: Calling the model on every keystroke can waste credits; a button press is better.
An app moved to another environment needs the model added again.
One Learn page marks this feature as preview, so check its status.

learn.title: Use AI Builder models in Power Apps

ppai-predict-action-dynamic-model.definition: A flow can pass a model ID in a variable, so it can pick a different document model for each file.

blocks.label: Predict action
blocks.plain: One flow action that can call many kinds of AI Builder models.

blocks.label: Model ID
blocks.plain: A value, held in a variable, that names the model to use.

blocks.label: Document type
blocks.plain: The kind of document that decides which model fits.

blocks.label: Request
blocks.plain: The file and its type, sent to the model with the call.

flow.label: File arrives
flow.plain: A file arrives in the flow.

flow.label: Decide
flow.plain: The flow decides which model suits that document.

flow.label: Set ID
flow.plain: It sets the model ID variable to that model.

flow.label: Predict
flow.plain: The Predict action runs the chosen model.

flow.label: Use
flow.plain: Later steps use the model output.

example.input: Fabrikam receives invoices in two different layouts.
example.output: The flow picks the model trained for each layout and runs it, so each invoice is read by the right model.

whenToUse: Different documents need different models.
The model should be chosen while the flow runs.
whenNot: Dynamic model IDs work for document processing, not for prompts.
Most flows do not need this. It is for complex cases.

learn.title: Use predict action in Power Automate

spai-autofill-columns.definition: An autofill column uses a plain-language prompt to get details from each file in a SharePoint library and save them.

blocks.label: Prompt
blocks.plain: The question you ask of each file, such as the due date.

blocks.label: Column
blocks.plain: The library column that stores the answer.

blocks.label: Test
blocks.plain: You can try the prompt on a sample file before saving it.

blocks.label: New files
blocks.plain: After setup, new files are processed automatically.

blocks.label: Check
blocks.plain: A person reviews results, because they might be wrong.

flow.label: Add file
flow.plain: Someone adds a file to the library.

flow.label: Read
flow.plain: The AI reads the file's text and answers each autofill prompt.

flow.label: Save
flow.plain: The answer is saved in the matching column.

flow.label: Existing files
flow.plain: Files that were already there can be processed on request.

flow.label: Review
flow.plain: A person checks the results.

example.input: A Contoso library holds contracts, and the prompt asks for the renewal date.
example.output: Each contract gets a renewal date in its own column, ready for sorting and search.

whenToUse: You want columns filled in without building a trained model.
Your questions are simple, such as dates, names, or choices.
whenNot: Learn suggests no more than 65 pages per file and 10 columns per library.
A changed file is processed again only when a person reprocesses it.

learn.title: Overview of autofill columns
Create an autofill column

spai-prebuilt-document-processing.definition: Ready-made models read common documents, such as invoices and contracts, with no training needed.

blocks.label: Prebuilt model
blocks.plain: Ready-made for contracts, invoices, receipts, and more.

blocks.label: Custom model
blocks.plain: Trained by your team for layouts that prebuilt models miss.

blocks.label: Content type
blocks.plain: The set of columns a model fills in for a library.

blocks.label: Billing
blocks.plain: Pay-as-you-go through a linked Azure subscription.

blocks.label: Site scope
blocks.plain: An organization can limit it to selected sites.

flow.label: Pick
flow.plain: Someone picks a prebuilt model that matches the documents in a library.

flow.label: Apply
flow.plain: They apply it to the library, linked to a content type.

flow.label: Extract
flow.plain: Files are read, and the model saves details to columns.

flow.label: Bill
flow.plain: Use is billed through the Azure subscription.

flow.label: Limit
flow.plain: An organization can turn it off or limit it to chosen sites.

example.input: Fabrikam's finance team keeps invoices in one library.
example.output: An invoice model fills columns such as customer name, due date, and amount due for each invoice.

whenToUse: Your files are common business documents, such as invoices.
You want results without collecting training examples.
whenNot: It needs pay-as-you-go billing set up first.
Unusual layouts may need a custom model.

learn.title: Set up and manage prebuilt document processing
Overview of document processing model types

ppai-document-processing-model.definition: An AI Builder document processing model learns where your fields sit from a few sample documents, then reads new documents of that kind.

blocks.label: Fields to find
blocks.plain: The fields, tables, and checkboxes you want the model to extract.

blocks.label: Collection
blocks.plain: A group of sample documents that share the same layout.

blocks.label: Training
blocks.plain: The step where the model learns from at least five samples per layout.

blocks.label: Publish
blocks.plain: Makes the trained model available to others in the environment.

blocks.label: Flow call
blocks.plain: A flow or app sends new documents to the published model.

flow.label: Define
flow.plain: A maker lists what to extract.

flow.label: Add samples
flow.plain: They add sample documents, grouped by layout.

flow.label: Train
flow.plain: They train the model, then try it with a quick test.

flow.label: Publish
flow.plain: They publish it.

flow.label: Use
flow.plain: A flow or app sends new documents and gets fields back.

example.input: Contoso has a vendor form that always has the same layout.
example.output: After training on five samples and publishing, a flow reads new forms and returns the fields the maker named.

whenToUse: Your documents have a layout that prebuilt models do not cover.
You can supply at least five sample documents per layout.
whenNot: A prebuilt model may already fit common documents such as invoices.
Training takes time, and general-document models train more slowly.

learn.title: Create a document processing custom model
Document processing model overview

ppai-category-classification-model.definition: Category classification learns from text you have tagged, then sorts new text into your own groups.

blocks.label: Tagged text
blocks.plain: Text entries with tags, stored in Dataverse.

blocks.label: Categories
blocks.plain: Your own labels, such as topics or request types.

blocks.label: Model
blocks.plain: Learns from your tags in the language you choose.

blocks.label: Published model
blocks.plain: The version a flow can call to tag new text.

flow.label: Prepare
flow.plain: A maker prepares text with tags in Dataverse.

flow.label: Create
flow.plain: They create the model, pointing it at the text and the tags.

flow.label: Train
flow.plain: They pick the language and train the model.

flow.label: Publish
flow.plain: They publish the model.

flow.label: Categorize
flow.plain: A flow calls it to categorize new text.

example.input: Contoso tags support emails as billing, shipping, or returns.
example.output: After training and publishing, the model gives new emails one of those tags, with confidence scores.

whenToUse: You need to route text by your own categories.
You already have tagged text to learn from.
whenNot: The training text must be in Dataverse, with tags, before you start.
A prebuilt model may be enough for general topics.

learn.title: Overview of the category classification custom model
Create a category classification custom model

ppai-prediction-model.definition: A prediction model learns from past records in Dataverse, then guesses the outcome for new ones: yes or no, a choice, or a number.

blocks.label: Historical outcome
blocks.plain: The column that holds the known answer, such as late or on time.

blocks.label: Training columns
blocks.plain: Columns the model learns from. Leave out any that give away the answer.

blocks.label: Filter
blocks.plain: An optional filter to train on part of the data.

blocks.label: Predictions
blocks.plain: Predicted outcomes for rows where the answer is not known yet.

flow.label: Choose outcome
flow.plain: A maker picks the table and the outcome column.

flow.label: Pick columns
flow.plain: They pick training columns and avoid target leakage.

flow.label: Filter
flow.plain: They filter the data if they need to.

flow.label: Train
flow.plain: They train and publish the model.

flow.label: Predict
flow.plain: The model predicts outcomes for new records.

example.input: Contoso wants to know whether a shipment will arrive on time.
example.output: The model learns from past shipments. It must not use the delivered date, because new shipments will not have one yet.

whenToUse: You have a history of records with known outcomes.
You want yes or no, a choice among options, or a number.
whenNot: You need Dataverse data: at least 50 rows, and 1,000 or more is better.
Columns that reveal the answer make the model look better than it is.

learn.title: Overview of the prediction model
Create a prediction model

spai-manage-copilot-availability.definition: Site owners use Site AI settings to manage Copilot in SharePoint, and Restricted Content Discovery hides AI on chosen sites.

blocks.label: Site AI settings
blocks.plain: Owners choose which agent opens and can hide the Copilot button.

blocks.label: Restricted discovery
blocks.plain: When on, Copilot and AI actions do not appear on the site.

blocks.label: Older controls
blocks.plain: Preview-era controls are retiring. Learn gives the date.

flow.label: Available
flow.plain: Copilot in SharePoint is available to licensed people on sites.

flow.label: Owner choices
flow.plain: A site owner can change which agent opens or hide the Copilot button.

flow.label: Restrict
flow.plain: An admin can limit discovery on risky sites.

flow.label: Hidden
flow.plain: On those sites, Copilot and AI actions do not appear.

flow.label: Retire
flow.plain: Older preview controls stop working after the date Learn gives.

example.input: A Contoso HR site holds sensitive files and is under review.
example.output: Copilot and AI actions are hidden on that site, whatever other settings say.

whenToUse: A site needs extra review before AI is used on it.
Visitors should not see the Copilot button on a site.
whenNot: Restricted Content Discovery does not change who can open files.
Do not rely on the older preview controls after they retire.

learn.title: Get started with Copilot in SharePoint
Restrict discovery of SharePoint sites and content
